reason: The text explicitly establishes and reinforces strict hierarchical structures at multiple levels: God commands Moses with absolute authority; Moses is positioned above Aaron ('you shall be as God to him'); the people must obey their leaders. When Moses questions his assigned role in the hierarchy, God becomes angry ('וַיִּֽחַר־ אַף יְהוָה בְּמֹשֶׁה'), demonstrating that acceptance of hierarchy is required, not optional. The passage culminates with the people worshipping and acknowledging the hierarchical authority of Moses and the leaders who deliver God's message. Even the physical setting emphasizes hierarchy—Moses must remove his sandals on holy ground, demonstrating respect for sacred boundaries. The entire narrative arc reinforces that hierarchy is central to the covenant relationship, not peripheral to it.
